key_insight: Mixing five A-site and seven B-site cations in one perovskite solid solution lets researchers tune magnetic ordering, with ferrimagnetic transitions still appearing between 89 and 115 K.
engineering_relevance: The study shows composition and size-disorder engineering can be used to adjust ordering temperatures in complex perovskite oxides, offering a design rule for functional oxide synthesis.
method: Synthesized single-phase AM7O3 perovskites with 12 cations on A and M sites.
Compared bulk magnetometry for A = La, Gd, La1/2Gd1/2, and the 5-cation A-site solid solution.
Related magnetic behavior to A-site radius, size disorder, and valence-electron count.
evidence_signal: Bulk magnetometry measurements show all tested compounds order magnetically as ferrimagnets within a relatively narrow 89–115 K range.
watch_item: The trend is based on a limited set of compositions, so broader validation is needed before generalizing the tuning rule across other complex perovskites.
paper_title: Varying A-site radius and size disorder to tune magnetic ordering in compositionally complex perovskite oxides
